tools.name: unreal_health_check
tools.title: Unreal Health Check
tools.description: Check connectivity to the Unreal Engine Remote Control API.

tools.name: ping_unreal
tools.title: Ping Unreal
tools.description: Pre-flight check: verify that a running Unreal Engine instance is reachable on the configured Remote Control API port. Call this before other Unreal tools to confirm connectivity and measure latency.

tools.name: list_unreal_instances
tools.title: List Unreal Instances
tools.description: Discover running Unreal editors (same payload as `simul unreal instances`). Each instance: reachable, latency_ms, error, editor identity (pid, instance_id, project_name, project_path, map_path, viewports, dirty_map_packages; null when its Python does not answer), active (Unreal tools target it) and attached (the saved `simul unreal attach` selection). Ports that do not answer are omitted, except the active one.

scan.description: When True, probe the configured port range plus the configured and attached ports concurrently. When False, probe only the active endpoint.

tools.name: capture_unreal_viewport
tools.title: Capture Unreal Viewport
tools.description: Capture a viewport screenshot via HighResScreenshot and return its path on the editor host. Pass inline=true to also receive the image itself as an image content block; captures above the inline size cap return the path alone.

format.description: Image format (png). Use CLI capture to convert to JPEG.

inline.description: Also return the image as an image content block.

tools.name: execute_unreal_script
tools.title: Execute Unreal Script
tools.description: Execute arbitrary Python code inside the Unreal Engine editor. Use for operations not covered by other tools. The code runs via PythonScriptLibrary.ExecutePythonCommandEx. Print JSON to return structured data. UE 5.7 hazard: do not leave a reference to an unreal static-library function (e.g. unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary.*, unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.*) or a struct method (e.g. unreal.Vector.length) in a reference cycle; a later garbage collection, including the editor's own on autosave, crashes the editor. Call them inline. For granular CLI operations see: simul unreal --help

tools.name: control_unreal_ui
tools.title: Control Unreal Ui
tools.description: Named controls in the explicitly attached Unreal editor: inspect, select actors, edit transforms, pilot/eject actors, set game view, and show per-agent overlay cursors. Requires simul unreal attach.

agent_control.description: inspect, select_actor, clear_selection, set_property, pilot_actor, eject_actor, set_game_view, move_cursor, or clear_cursor.

target.description: Actor full path or unique label; otherwise the sole selected actor.

value.description: Three finite numbers for set_property; location is in cm.

agent_id.description: Stable agent label; supply a unique value for each concurrent agent.

position.description: move_cursor only: normalized [x,y] from bottom-left; defaults to center.

activity.description: move_cursor only: short label describing the current work.

tools.name: get_unreal_engine_info
tools.title: Get Unreal Engine Info
tools.description: Get Unreal Engine runtime information.

tools.name: get_unreal_loaded_map
tools.title: Get Unreal Loaded Map
tools.description: Get the currently loaded persistent level path.

tools.name: list_unreal_actors
tools.title: List Unreal Actors
tools.description: List actors in the current Unreal Engine level with optional class and tag filters.

class_filter.description: Filter by UClass name (empty string = no filter).

tag_filter.description: Filter by actor tag (empty string = no filter).

max_results.description: Maximum number of actors to return.

tools.name: get_unreal_actor_info
tools.title: Get Unreal Actor Info
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific actor including transform, components, and tags. The path must name a live actor of the level open in the editor; a deleted actor, or one of a map that is not open, is not found, and no map is loaded to look for it.

actor_path.description: Full object path of the actor.

tools.name: search_unreal_assets
tools.title: Search Unreal Assets
tools.description: Search the Unreal Asset Registry by name, class, or package path.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results, from 1 to 1000.

tools.name: describe_unreal_object
tools.title: Describe Unreal Object
tools.description: Get full property and function metadata for any UObject by path.

tools.name: get_unreal_actor_thumbnail
tools.title: Get Unreal Actor Thumbnail
tools.description: Get a thumbnail image for an Unreal asset. The image arrives as an MCP image content block, followed by a JSON block with asset_path, format, width, height and image_attached=true.

tools.name: summarize_unreal_scene
tools.title: Summarize Unreal Scene
tools.description: Generate an LLM-friendly digest of the current Unreal scene.

tools.name: get_unreal_viewport_info
tools.title: Get Unreal Viewport Info
tools.description: Get active viewport camera and render information.

tools.name: set_unreal_camera_view
tools.title: Set Unreal Camera View
tools.description: Set the editor viewport camera position and rotation and return the camera read back. Each axis of location within 4398046511104 cm (2^42) of the origin and pitch from -90 to 90 degrees, the furthest Unreal takes; a group left out keeps its value.

tools.name: focus_unreal_on_actor
tools.title: Focus Unreal On Actor
tools.description: Focus the editor viewport camera on a specific actor and make it the whole selection. With distance 0 the camera looks at the center of the actor's bounds and backs off until they fit a view fov degrees across and aspect_ratio wide per unit of height: by default UE's default 90-degree field of view on the 16:9 of the default capture. Editor Python cannot read the viewport's field of view, so pass fov when it was changed, and aspect_ratio for a capture of another shape. distance reports the distance used, and fit_warning says when an actor without bounds got the default 500 cm. selected reports whether Unreal selected it. While PIE runs, Unreal's editor selects nothing, so the camera moves but selected is false, with pie_active true and a warning.

actor_path.description: Full actor path to focus on.

distance.description: How far behind the actor the camera stands, in cm, rising half as far and looking down at it (0 or less = auto-fit to the actor's bounds).

fov.description: Auto-fit only: field of view across the view, in degrees, at least 0.001 (the narrowest Unreal renders) and less than 180. The level viewport's; UE's default is 90.

aspect_ratio.description: Auto-fit only: the view's width over its height, from 1/16384 to 16384, such as a capture's resolution_x / resolution_y; 16:9 by default, as the default 1920x1080 capture.

tools.name: spawn_unreal_actor
tools.title: Spawn Unreal Actor
tools.description: Spawn an actor from a class or asset path, with its label, in one undoable editor transaction; the label and transform are read back. Refused: a class Unreal does not let you place (the level's WorldSettings and other per-level singletons, game-framework classes such as GameModeBase or PlayerController, a bare Brush), an abstract class, a map or an actor in a level, and a label Unreal would not take (leading or trailing whitespace, over 1023 characters, 'None').

asset_path.description: Asset or class path to spawn from.

location_x.description: Spawn X position in Unreal units (cm).

location_y.description: Spawn Y position in Unreal units (cm).

location_z.description: Spawn Z position in Unreal units (cm); Unreal is Z-up.

rotation_pitch.description: Spawn pitch in degrees (rotation about Y).

rotation_yaw.description: Spawn yaw in degrees (rotation about Z).

rotation_roll.description: Spawn roll in degrees (rotation about X).

label.description: Optional actor label in the outliner: no leading or trailing whitespace, at most 1023 characters, not 'None'.

tools.name: delete_unreal_actor
tools.title: Delete Unreal Actor
tools.description: Delete an actor from the level, in one undoable editor transaction. DESTRUCTIVE operation. A path that names no actor of the level open in the editor (or a label) is NotFoundError; the level's WorldSettings, its builder brush and other actors the editor keeps out of the Outliner are refused.

actor_path.description: Full actor path, as list_unreal_actors reports it.

tools.name: set_unreal_actor_transform
tools.title: Set Unreal Actor Transform
tools.description: Set an actor's world location, rotation and/or scale. Each is optional; one left out keeps its current value. Returns the transform read back.

location.description: World position [x, y, z] in Unreal units (cm); Unreal is Z-up. Omit to keep the current location.

rotation.description: World rotation [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees: pitch about Y, yaw about Z, roll about X. Omit to keep the current rotation.

scale.description: Scale factors [x, y, z]; 1.0 is unscaled. Omit to keep the current scale.

tools.name: set_unreal_actor_property
tools.title: Set Unreal Actor Property
tools.description: Set a property on an Unreal actor by name and JSON value.

generate_transaction.description: Whether to generate an undo transaction.

tools.name: call_unreal_actor_function
tools.title: Call Unreal Actor Function
tools.description: Call a BlueprintCallable UFUNCTION on an actor of the level open in the editor, as one undo step that records the actor and its root component first.

tools.name: set_unreal_actor_parent
tools.title: Set Unreal Actor Parent
tools.description: Attach an actor to a parent actor (parent_path), or detach it from its parent (detach=true with an empty parent_path). The actor keeps its world transform, the change is one undoable editor transaction, and the parent is read back: parent_path is the parent afterwards (null once detached), with previous_parent_path and changed. Attaching an actor to itself or under one of its own children, or a Static actor under a parent that is not Static, is refused with the reason, as is a path that names no actor of the level open in the editor.

actor_path.description: Full path of the actor to attach or detach.

parent_path.description: Full path of the actor to attach it to; an empty string together with detach=true.

detach.description: Detach the actor from its parent instead, keeping its world transform.

tools.name: add_unreal_component
tools.title: Add Unreal Component
tools.description: Add an instance component to an actor in the level, as the editor's Add Component button does, in one undoable editor transaction. A scene component attaches under parent_component or the root component. Returns the component read back: component_path, component_name, component_class, parent_component and is_root. Abstract classes and names already used inside the actor are refused.

component_class.description: Component class: a native class name such as PointLightComponent, or a class path such as /Script/Engine.PointLightComponent or a Blueprint component's /Game/BP_Lamp.BP_Lamp_C.

component_name.description: Name of the new component, unique inside the actor, without spaces or punctuation such as . : / ( ); empty lets Unreal name it after its class.

parent_component.description: Name of the actor's scene component to attach the new one under (get_unreal_actor_info lists the components); empty attaches it under the root component. Scene components only.

tools.name: set_unreal_actor_visibility
tools.title: Set Unreal Actor Visibility
tools.description: Show or hide an actor, in one undoable editor transaction, and read every flag back. scope 'editor' is the editor's hide (the Outliner's eye): the level viewport and captures honour it, and it lasts the editor session unless persistent also sets the hidden-at-editor-startup flag saved with the level. scope 'game' is hidden in game, saved with the level: Play In Editor and the packaged game honour it, the level viewport still draws the actor. 'all' (the default) sets both. propagate applies the same to every actor attached under it. actors lists each actor's hidden_in_editor, hidden_in_editor_at_startup and hidden_in_game read back.

visible.description: Show the actor (true) or hide it (false).

propagate.description: Apply the same to every actor attached under it, children of children included; a hidden parent hides none of them.

scope.description: Which visibility to set: 'editor' (level viewport and captures), 'game' (Play In Editor and the packaged game) or 'all'.

persistent.description: Editor scopes only: also set the hidden-at-editor-startup flag saved with the level, so the editor hiding outlasts a reload. Not while Play In Editor runs.

tools.name: get_unreal_material_info
tools.title: Get Unreal Material Info
tools.description: Get a Material's or Material Instance's scalar, vector and texture parameters with their values (an instance's: the value it renders with, and whether it overrides it), its parent and base material, material domain and blend mode. A parameter inside the material's Material Layers is listed for its layer or blend (association and index), with that layer's value.

material_path.description: Material or Material Instance asset path, e.g. /Game/Materials/MI_Wood.

tools.name: set_unreal_material_params
tools.title: Set Unreal Material Params
tools.description: Set scalar, vector and texture parameters on a Material Instance Constant (left unsaved) and read them back; applied holds the values read back. Only global parameters are set: the call fails, writing nothing, when the material has no global parameter by a given name (a name only its Material Layers have included) or a texture does not load, and fails when a value reads back different, keeping what applied; not_applied gives each reason. An instance outside /Game (engine or plugin content) is refused unless allow_engine_content is true.

scalar_params_json.description: JSON object of scalar parameter name to float value, e.g. '{"Roughness": 0.4}'. Empty string sets none.

vector_params_json.description: JSON object of vector parameter name to an [R, G, B, A] list of floats ([R, G, B] sets alpha 1). Empty string sets none.

texture_params_json.description: JSON object of texture parameter name to a texture asset path. Empty string sets none.

allow_engine_content.description: Also write to content outside the project's /Game folder: /Engine or a plugin's content, which every project using that engine or plugin shares. Default false refuses it (SandboxError).

tools.name: create_unreal_material_instance
tools.title: Create Unreal Material Instance
tools.description: Create and save a Material Instance Constant from a parent material, in the project's /Game folder: save_path, else the parent's folder when it is in /Game, else /Game/Materials. A folder outside /Game is refused unless allow_engine_content is true.

parent_path.description: Parent material (or material instance) asset path.

save_path.description: Content folder for the new instance, such as /Game/Materials. Empty picks the parent's folder when it is under /Game, else /Game/Materials.

allow_engine_content.description: Also write to content outside the project's /Game folder: /Engine or a plugin's content, which every project using that engine or plugin shares. Default false refuses it (SandboxError).

tools.name: assign_unreal_material
tools.title: Assign Unreal Material
tools.description: Assign a material to a mesh component's material slot of an actor in the level being edited, as one undoable transaction that marks the level dirty, and read it back.

tools.name: set_unreal_light_params
tools.title: Set Unreal Light Params
tools.description: Set light component parameters (intensity, color, temperature, shadows); a parameter left out keeps its current value.

color.description: Light color as [r, g, b], each channel 0-1; None keeps the current color.

use_temperature.description: Use color temperature instead of direct color.

attenuation_radius.description: Light attenuation radius in cm (point and spot lights only).

tools.name: set_unreal_render_settings
tools.title: Set Unreal Render Settings
tools.description: Set one numeric rendering console variable (r.* or sg.*, e.g. r.ScreenPercentage 75) and read it back. applied is true only when the variable holds the value afterwards. A variable Unreal does not have fails with NotFoundError and changes nothing; a value Unreal did not take (a read-only variable such as r.RayTracing, which only startup config sets, or one it limits) fails with RenderSettingNotApplied, giving value and previous_value. Post-process settings live on PostProcessVolume actors, not in console variables, so this tool does not change them.

setting_name.description: Console variable name, r.* or sg.* (r.ScreenPercentage).

tools.name: control_unreal_simulation
tools.title: Control Unreal Simulation
tools.description: Control Play-In-Editor: start, stop, pause or resume. Exact frame stepping is unsupported. While PIE runs, Unreal's editor spawns and deletes no actors, so those tools return PIEActive until it stops; level reads keep working and report pie_active.

action.description: One of start, stop, pause, resume, step.

tools.name: get_unreal_simulation_status
tools.title: Get Unreal Simulation Status
tools.description: Get current Play-In-Editor simulation status (playing, paused, stopped).

tools.name: enable_unreal_physics
tools.title: Enable Unreal Physics
tools.description: Make an actor's body simulate physics (falls, takes forces), make it kinematic (physics collision, moved only by its transform), or turn physics off, in one undoable editor transaction that marks the map dirty. A Static body is made Movable unless make_movable is false; a body without physics collision or simple collision geometry is refused (IncompatibleBody, with the reasons). Unreal detaches a simulated body from its parent, so an attached one needs allow_detach. Returns the body read back: physics_mode, mobility, collision and mass.

enable.description: True makes the body physical: simulated, or kinematic with kinematic true. False stops it simulating, keeping its collision and mobility.

kinematic.description: With enable true, make the body kinematic instead of simulated: it keeps physics collision, so simulated bodies hit it, but is not simulated and moves only when its transform is set.

make_movable.description: Make a Static or Stationary body Movable, which simulation and kinematic movement need (reported as mobility_changed_from); false refuses such a body instead.

allow_detach.description: Let a body attached to a parent be detached from it as it starts simulating, keeping its world transform, as Unreal does (reported as detached_from; Undo reattaches it, turning physics off does not). False refuses an attached body.

tools.name: set_unreal_collision
tools.title: Set Unreal Collision
tools.description: Set an actor's collision preset and/or enable or disable its collision, in one undoable editor transaction that marks the map dirty; what is left out is kept and an unknown preset changes nothing. Returns the state read back.

collision_preset.description: Named collision preset (e.g. BlockAll, PhysicsActor, OverlapAll, NoCollision); empty keeps the current preset. An unknown preset changes nothing.

collision_enabled.description: True for query and physics collision, False for none. None keeps the collision mode the preset sets, or the current one when no preset is given. Overriding a preset's mode turns the preset into Custom.

tools.name: apply_unreal_force
tools.title: Apply Unreal Force
tools.description: Apply a force or impulse to an actor's physics body.

is_impulse.description: True for impulse, False for continuous force.

location_x.description: Application point X (None = center of mass).

tools.name: set_unreal_physics_params
tools.title: Set Unreal Physics Params
tools.description: Set physics body parameters (mass in kg, linear and angular damping, gravity) on an actor in one undoable editor transaction that marks the map dirty, and read them back; a parameter left out is kept. A Static body keeps the values but has no mass until it is Movable (see warning).

mass.description: Mass override in kg, from 0.001 (Unreal's least) to 1e9.

tools.name: import_unreal_usd
tools.title: Import Unreal Usd
tools.description: Import USD with Unreal's optional USDImporter plugin, enabled at editor startup: assets to <destination_path>/<file name>, and actors into the level being edited. Without replace_existing it is refused when that folder already holds assets, and existing actors are kept; with it, those assets and the level's actors from an earlier import of the file are replaced.

usd_path.description: Path to the USD file on disk; must be inside the sandbox.

import_options.description: Boolean USD options: import_actors, import_geometry, import_materials, import_lights, import_cameras.

replace_existing.description: Replace the assets already in <destination_path>/<file name> and the level's actors from an earlier import of this file. Default false refuses an import into a folder that holds assets (InvalidState) and replaces no actor.

tools.name: export_unreal_usd
tools.title: Export Unreal Usd
tools.description: Export actors of the level being edited with the optional USDImporter plugin's LevelExporterUSD; actors_exported counts the actors the written stage has a prim for.

actor_paths.description: Comma-separated actor object paths to export.

output_path.description: Output USD file path; must be inside the sandbox.

tools.name: convert_to_simready
tools.title: Convert To Simready
tools.description: Unavailable in Unreal: SimReady conversion returns UnsupportedOperation without writing files.

usd_path.description: Source USD file; must be inside the sandbox.

output_path.description: Output SimReady USD file path; must be inside the sandbox.

add_physics.description: Add physics schemas (rigid body) to the output.

add_semantic_labels.description: Attach semantic labels to the output prims.

target_up_axis.description: Up axis written to the output stage (Y or Z).

target_units.description: Unit system of the output stage (meters or centimeters).

tools.name: validate_simready_asset
tools.title: Validate Simready Asset
tools.description: Unavailable in Unreal: SimReady validation returns UnsupportedOperation.

usd_path.description: USD file path to validate; must be inside the sandbox.

checks.description: Comma-separated validation checks to run (physics, collision, materials, scale, up_axis, semantics). Empty string runs every check.

tools.name: get_unreal_interchange_info
tools.title: Get Unreal Interchange Info
tools.description: Query available Interchange pipelines and supported formats.

tools.name: batch_unreal_operations
tools.title: Batch Unreal Operations
tools.description: Execute several Remote Control requests in one HTTP call, in order. Each result is Remote Control's answer (RequestId, ResponseCode, ResponseBody); a failed one also has error and error_type. Operations without a RequestId are numbered for you.

operations.description: JSON array of operations: [{"URL": "/remote/object/call", "Verb": "PUT", "Body": {"objectPath": "...", "functionName": "..."}, "RequestId": 1}]. RequestId is optional and must be a unique integer.

tools.name: query_unreal_scene_graph
tools.title: Query Unreal Scene Graph
tools.description: Query the Unreal scene graph hierarchy.

root_path.description: Root actor path (None for level root).

tools.name: analyze_unreal_scene_for_robotics
tools.title: Analyze Unreal Scene For Robotics
tools.description: Classify level actors for robotics from their collision setup: floor-like surfaces a robot can stand on, small Movable objects it can grasp, and collision counts and problems (static meshes with physics collision but no simple shapes). Uses the bounding box of each actor's collision-enabled components; the thresholds come back as criteria.

analysis_types.description: Comma-separated analyses: traversability, graspability, collision_complexity. Empty runs all three.

actor_filter.description: Only analyze actors whose label or object path contains this text, ignoring case; empty or null analyzes every actor.

tools.name: generate_unreal_procedural_scene
tools.title: Generate Unreal Procedural Scene
tools.description: Build a room, corridor, warehouse or outdoor test scene from Engine basic shapes inside the bounds, in one undoable transaction; the same arguments give the same layout. Returns the spawned actor paths and the tag and outliner folder that group them, both unique to the call.

parameters.description: JSON object; lengths in cm, counts 0 to 200. Any type: seed (integer 0 to 4294967295, 42). room: wall_thickness (20), wall_height (bounds top), door_width (100, capped by the side walls; 0 for none), props (one per 16 m2 of floor). corridor: wall_thickness, wall_height, props (one per 3 m). warehouse: wall_thickness, wall_height, rows (as many as fit), shelf_depth (100), shelf_height (300, capped by the bounds), aisle_width (250), props (one per 16 m2 of free floor). outdoor: trees (one per 20 m2), rocks (one per 10 m2). Props are Movable boxes; everything else is Static.

bounds_min.description: Minimum corner as comma-separated x,y,z in cm; empty is 0,0,0.

bounds_max.description: Maximum corner as comma-separated x,y,z in cm; empty is 1000,1000,500.

tools.name: get_unreal_actor_by_semantic_label
tools.title: Get Unreal Actor By Semantic Label
tools.description: Find level actors whose actor tags match a label: exact, contains or regex, ignoring case.

label.description: Semantic label (actor tag) to search for.

match_mode.description: exact (a tag equals label), contains (a tag contains label) or regex (label is a Python regular expression searched for in each tag, ignoring case; a pattern whose failing search can run for long on a 1023-character tag is refused, such as a repeated group that holds a quantifier or alternatives, as in (\w+)+, or two quantifiers that can divide the same characters between them, as in .*.*x or A*a*x); every mode ignores case.

max_results.description: Maximum number of actors to return, 1 to 5000.

tools.name: generate_unreal_mesh_primitive
tools.title: Generate Unreal Mesh Primitive
tools.description: Create a parametric mesh primitive (box, sphere, cylinder, cone, torus, capsule).

primitive_type.description: box, sphere, cylinder, cone, torus, capsule.

location.description: Spawn location [x, y, z] in cm.

tools.name: apply_unreal_mesh_boolean
tools.title: Apply Unreal Mesh Boolean
tools.description: Apply boolean operation (union, subtract, intersect) between two meshes.

tools.name: compute_unreal_convex_hull
tools.title: Compute Unreal Convex Hull
tools.description: Compute convex hull envelope of a mesh.

tools.name: decompose_unreal_convex_hull
tools.title: Decompose Unreal Convex Hull
tools.description: V-HACD convex decomposition for collision geometry.

tools.name: edit_unreal_mesh_topology
tools.title: Edit Unreal Mesh Topology
tools.description: Edit mesh topology (extrude, bevel, inset, loop cut, scale_faces).

face_selection.description: Face selection filter (unused in current impl).

edge_selection.description: Edge selection filter (unused in current impl).

scale.description: Scale factors [x, y, z] (unused in current impl).

tools.name: subdivide_unreal_mesh
tools.title: Subdivide Unreal Mesh
tools.description: Catmull-Clark / Loop / bilinear subdivision.

tools.name: simplify_unreal_mesh
tools.title: Simplify Unreal Mesh
tools.description: Simplify/decimate a mesh to reduce triangle count.

tools.name: cut_unreal_mesh_plane
tools.title: Cut Unreal Mesh Plane
tools.description: Cut/slice a mesh along an arbitrary plane.

plane_origin.description: Plane origin [x, y, z] in cm.

keep_both_sides.description: Keep both halves (unused — UE plane cut keeps one side and optionally fills).

tools.name: validate_unreal_mesh
tools.title: Validate Unreal Mesh
tools.description: Validate mesh integrity (manifold, normals, degenerates, self-intersection).

checks.description: Checks to run (currently all checks always run).

tools.name: convert_unreal_mesh_format
tools.title: Convert Unreal Mesh Format
tools.description: Convert mesh between formats (static mesh, dynamic mesh, skeletal mesh).

tools.name: remesh_unreal_mesh
tools.title: Remesh Unreal Mesh
tools.description: Remesh a mesh (uniform, adaptive) to improve triangle quality.

tools.name: compute_unreal_mesh_uv
tools.title: Compute Unreal Mesh Uv
tools.description: Generate or recompute UV coordinates for a mesh.
